mod.description: Ten major cities and configurable rules for Spore's Civilization Stage.

component.description: Use the original vehicle prices.
Reduce vehicle prices by 25%.
Reduce vehicle prices by 50%.
Use the original 2-second firing interval.
Set the firing interval to 1.5 seconds.
Set the firing interval to 0.5 seconds.
Use the original vehicle speeds.
Increase land, sea and air vehicle speed by 25%.
Increase land, sea and air vehicle speed by 50%.
Use the default target of 8 offensive units during Civilization planet generation.
Set the offensive unit target to 12 during planet generation.
Set the offensive unit target to 16 during planet generation.
Each rival starts with a population of 15.
Each rival starts with a population of 30.
Rivals start with a population between 15 and 50.
Each rival starts with 4,000 Sporebucks.
Each rival starts with 8,000 Sporebucks.
Rivals start with between 4,000 and 15,000 Sporebucks.
Each rival has an equal chance of being military, religious or economic.
Start with exactly three military, three religious and three economic rivals.
Rivals have a 50/50 chance of being religious or economic.
Rivals have a 50/50 chance of being military or economic.
Rivals have a 50/50 chance of being military or religious.
All rivals start as military nations.
All rivals start as religious nations.
All rivals start as economic nations.
Use the original rules for city specialties after an AI capture.
Cities captured by a rival keep their old specialty. The player keeps the usual choice.
Use original turret and fleet limits. Large cities have 8 military, 6 religious or 4 economic turret slots.
On Hard, rivals aim for 8, 6 or 4 turrets by city type. Player and rival fleet caps rise by about 38% before rounding. Other difficulties use vanilla rules.
All large cities get 8 slots. On Hard, rivals aim to fill all 8. Fleet caps rise by about 85% on Hard, 33% on Normal and 50% on Easy.
An economic AI can open its first rival trade route to a reachable city when both sides are at least neutral. Deliveries and buyouts follow vanilla rules.
Use the original conditions for opening trade routes.
Land, sea and air traders stay on course after taking a hit while opening or serving a route. They can still take damage and be destroyed.
Use the original retreat behavior when traders are hit.
Keep native offensive target selection.

Experimental: after 2-4 failed groups of at least 3 units and 20 seconds without assigned attackers, try another native eligible city. Progress resets failures. Keep the current target if no alternative is found. History resets on load.
Do not write the optional AI diagnostic journal.
Record AI decisions, conversions and combat. Visible battles also get detailed movement, building targets and turret logs. Read-only, with bounded output.
Do not cancel continuously reinforced attacks. Independent of Offensive Targets.

Experimental: cancel identified city attack orders after 2 simulated minutes without a new capture/conversion gauge high. Starts near the city with at least 3 assigned units. Avoid that city for 2 minutes; native AI chooses any alternative. Reinforcements do not reset the timer. Applies to AI versus players and other AI; excludes forced diplomatic targets. History resets on load.

Experimental: same stalled-attack rule with a 3-minute delay. A new gauge high resets the delay; turret losses alone do not. Avoid the city for 2 minutes after canceling identified attack orders. No forced return home. Independent of Offensive Targets; history resets on load.

Experimental: same stalled-attack rule with a 4-minute delay and a 2-minute target cooldown. More time to make net conquest/conversion progress before canceling identified attack orders. Independent of Offensive Targets; history resets on load.
Keep native vehicle movement without extra retries.

Previous experiment: retry the same local destination after sustained immobility. Did not resolve the reported naval congestion. Visible land and sea combat vehicles only; no active weapon target or recent firing. Orders stay intact. Two retries per episode, 20 seconds apart.

Experimental: detect blocked approaches after 8 seconds or quiet loops after 20 seconds. Includes sea and air traders. A genuinely idle land/sea blocker may yield, including player units. Up to two checked detour legs; explicit orders and combat take priority. Aircraft keep their altitude. Enable AI Diagnostics.
Do not add automatic retirement for ships without a port.

EXPERIMENTAL, AI only: after losing all ports, idle combat ships first try to capture an enemy port on the same sea. Idle economic ships and combat ships without an eligible port may be sold after 2 safe minutes, at most one per nation every 30 seconds. Preserve active combat missions and player fleets. Impossible sea trade requests are cancelled by the native behavior. Timers reset on load.
Keep native decisions about selling surplus land vehicles.

Experimental, AI only: after 3 idle minutes, sell surplus combat land units when the fleet has at least 32 units, no hostile city is on their continent, and an enemy port is reachable across the same sea from a matching-specialty port. Keep 6 ground defenders per owned city on that continent. Stop at 6 ships of that specialty; normal AI still chooses purchases. One sale per nation per 30 seconds.
